changes: Renamed the CLI from `lattice` to `proof-or-stop` under a two-tier freeze rule. RENAMED (no bearing on past evidence): user-facing bin name, docs, CLAUDE.md, agent prompt templates, commit subjects (`proof-or-stop:`), version-bump messages, acceptance-topology wrapper recognition, and every user-visible env-var name in help text and diagnostics. FROZEN (load-bearing on past evidence): signature salts, `.lattice/` paths, `LATTICE_*` env keys as STORED keys, and the 13 `lattice-*` agent role IDs — renaming any of these would invalidate historical signatures or break in-flight story spawns. Multi-developer safety comes from a read-both contract: every recognizer accepts BOTH names, so a teammate whose branch still emits `lattice:` keeps working after merge. Key sites: core/brand-env.ts (additive resolver, canonical wins), core/auto-commit-metadata.ts, handlers/validate-channel.ts (the runtime had been rejecting its own commits), core/acceptance-topology.ts (recognizer was backwards), core/version-bump.ts, core/lattice-dispatch.ts. Added a three-check residue gate (koala / brand-prose / brand-exec) covering docs, host adapter mirrors, and the executable surface — none of which any gate had scanned before.
usage: Run `proof-or-stop <command>` wherever you previously ran `lattice <command>`; e.g. `proof-or-stop session_brief`, `proof-or-stop validate --story=B-xxxx`. The old `lattice` bin still resolves, both commit-subject forms are still recognized, and both env-var spellings still resolve (canonical wins when both are set), so a teammate merging an older branch needs no migration step. `proof-or-stop --version` prints 0.3.254.
expectedOutcome: A user typing `proof-or-stop session_brief` gets exactly what `lattice session_brief` gave; docs, help text and agent prompts teach only the new name; and a teammate merging a branch that still writes `lattice:` commit subjects or sets `LATTICE_*` env vars passes every gate unchanged.
actualTranscript: `proof-or-stop --version` -> Proof-or-Stop 0.3.254. Both bin entrypoints resolve identically (28/28 entrypoint checks pass). Read-both verified by execution: readBrandEnv with LATTICE_AGENT -> old value, with PROOF_OR_STOP_AGENT -> new value, both set -> canonical wins. `proof-or-stop finding_add --help` now prints PROOF_OR_STOP_AGENT where it printed LATTICE_AGENT. Root suite `npm test` exit 0 (226s). validate 94/94 allPass:true. done_closure 16/16 PASS. The three smokes previously red on pristine main (prompt-token-cost, proofstory-acceptance-topology, lattice-cli-migration) were re-run at DONE time and now all PASS.
outcomeDiff: No difference from expectation. Everything the story committed to is delivered: 6/6 checklist items done, 36 verification evidence rows, 71 findings all resolved or dismissed (0 open), 16/16 closure checks PASS. Two caveats recorded earlier no longer hold or were never in scope: (1) the three red smokes cited in the first draft of this summary now PASS — they were pre-existing failures on main, since fixed by intervening main merges, and were re-run at DONE time to confirm; (2) the framework gaps logged to B-META-framework-audit (F-021..F-035) were never part of this storys scope — they are defects in other subsystems (validate --concept matching, managed-asset ownership predicates, dist/ rebuild races) found incidentally while working, and were escalated rather than fixed because changing those subsystems mid-rename would alter the very gates judging this story. No deliverable was dropped, narrowed, or deferred.
limitations: (1) The 13 `lattice-*` agent role IDs are deliberately NOT renamed — they are subagent_type values and renaming them would break in-flight story spawns; the target `proof-or-stop-*` prefix is owned by proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md. (2) Signature salts, `.lattice/` directories and `LATTICE_*` env keys as stored keys stay frozen by design so historical evidence keeps verifying; only their user-visible presentation was renamed. (3) `__LATTICE_WS_PORT` / `LATTICE_SHELL` remain — they are hardcoded protocol-level identifiers across five source files, a protocol change rather than a diagnostics edit, and are a disclosed follow-up. (4) Assurance is degraded-single-host (3x1) rather than the full 3x2 quorum: the second independent host was hard-blocked on usage limits and the third canonical host is empirically unusable; recorded explicitly via review_escalation_fallback_set with the reduction stated, not waived.
pitfalls: Cost me repeatedly, worth reading before the next rename-shaped story: (1) My own approximating regex is not the gate. I reported ~108 residue hits as measured when the gate counted 161/84. Run the gate function, never an eyeball grep. (2) Grepping `lattice: ` with a colon looked thorough but was structurally blind to `chore: bump lattice cli to` — 205 historical instances. (3) Excluding smoke|test from sweeps missed a 4th copy of a duplicated rule; a test that recomputes expected content rots exactly like production. (4) One AST fingerprint had TWO pinned copies and the coupling was documented in the comment directly above the literal — I still repinned only one. Grep the old digest repo-wide before editing either. (5) THE BIG ONE: a rename can break the CANONICAL name. Four findings (F-061, F-062, F-065, F-068) were comparisons or parsers hardcoding the deprecated literal, so the NEW spelling silently failed while the old one worked — exactly backwards. I never found one of these myself; the reviewer found all four across five consecutive rounds. Sweep for brand literals inside decisions, not just inside output. (6) Two predicates (F-066, F-067) tested for a literal the generator never emits because it builds names by concatenation — dead checks that never fired. (7) Raising timeout budgets to clear a watchdog caused three separate failures: budgets are load-bearing evidence, and an exported PROOF_OR_STOP_* value outranks a test harness LATTICE_*-only pin inside spawned children. (8) Do not edit material mid-review-round; it cost an entire completed reviewer lane. (9) Never conclude GREEN or RED from a run made while another worktree is hammering the box.
